stemBlocks.value: Make h the subject of the formula V = πr²h (the volume of a cylinder).
Think first: h is multiplied by the whole quantity πr², so divide by that quantity as one block.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p096-q10 from workbook page 96.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide both sides by πr² in a single step.

whyThisWorks.value: Although πr² contains a squared letter, it is a single multiplying factor as far as h is concerned, so one division removes all of it. Because r is not the subject here, the square never has to be undone.

commonErrors.misconception: Square-rooting unnecessarily because of the r².
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Square-rooting unnecessarily because of the r².

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by πr instead of πr².
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by πr instead of πr².

commonErrors.misconception: Writing h = V/π r² ambiguously without brackets.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing h = V/π r² ambiguously without brackets.

examTip.value: Before rearranging, underline the subject — everything not underlined is a coefficient to be divided away in one move.
